input.description: Roblox video rules and recording
input.prompt:
Web research task (read-only; do not create or modify any files; return findings as text). Today is 2026-11-13. I am writing a technical report for someone who will make monetized YouTube Shorts animated inside Roblox Studio. I need verified facts with exact URLs and, for policy text, VERBATIM English quotes (short, the exact governing sentences). Clearly label each item as (a) official Roblox/OBS/YouTube source, (b) community report (DevForum, Reddit, blogs), or (c) could not verify. Do not guess; if a page cannot be fetched say so.

PART 1: Roblox rules about using Roblox Studio footage, avatars and catalog (Marketplace/UGC) items in monetized YouTube videos. Find and quote the currently valid official texts:
- "Roblox Name and Logo Community Usage Guidelines" (try https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001708126 and search the help center) : what it says about videos, channel names using "Roblox"/"Blox", logo use, required disclaimers.
- Roblox Terms of Use sections about recording/streaming/videos of Roblox content and commercial use (https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846-Roblox-Terms-of-Use), including any licence to create videos ("Roblox videos", "machinima", "UGC licence") and any limits (e.g. cannot charge to view, ad revenue allowed).
- DevForum post "Update to Roblox Licensing Program / Brand Guidelines" https://devforum.roblox.com/t/update-to-roblox-licensing-program-brand-guidelines/1843674 : quote the FAQ lines about YouTube videos and monetization.
- Anything official about using other creators' Marketplace items (UGC clothing/accessories, classic faces) or Creator Store models/audio in videos outside Roblox. Note especially audio licensing (Roblox catalog audio is licensed only for use inside Roblox experiences; find the official statement).
- Roblox Community Standards items relevant to story videos featuring avatars (e.g. romantic content, real brands). Just the pointer and a one-line quote.

PART 2: Recording Roblox Studio.
- Roblox Studio built-in video recorder ("Record Video" in Studio / File menu or View tab): what official docs say (format, resolution, limits; whether it still exists in 2026 Studio). Search create.roblox.com/docs and DevForum.
- Engine APIs for capture: `CaptureService` (CaptureScreenshot, StartVideoCaptureAsync or similar) per https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/CaptureService : is there a video capture API, max duration (I believe 30 s), does it work in Studio, where do files go. Quote the doc.
- Any official or community way to render Roblox scenes to video offline / frame by frame without screen recording (e.g. Moon Animator export, Studio "video_capture" MCP tool, ViewportFrame tricks). Label confidence.
- OBS Studio recommended recording settings for capturing a game window at 60 fps on Windows 11 from official OBS docs/knowledge base (obsproject.com/kb): capture source type (Game Capture vs Window Capture, which works with Roblox Studio which is a Qt/D3D11 app), recorder encoder (NVENC/AMF/QSV/x264), rate control (CQP/CRF values), container (MKV vs MP4, hybrid MP4), base/output canvas resolution, how to set a custom vertical or large canvas, FPS setting. Quote key recommendations with URLs.
- OBS automation: obs-websocket (built in since OBS 28, default port 4455) requests StartRecord/StopRecord, so a script can start recording right before triggering the scene. Confirm from official obs-websocket protocol docs with URL.

PART 3: Roblox Studio minimum system requirements (official: https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/setup and the include file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/includes/studio/system-reqs.md ; also the help-center article). Quote the list exactly.

Output format: a structured list per part; each bullet = claim + label (official/community/unverified) + URL + verbatim quote where it is policy text. Keep the whole answer under about 1500 words.

    description: |
      The internal `Datatype.CFrame` that is manipulated when a `Class.Motor6D`
      is being animated. It is recommended to use this property for custom
      animations rather than `Class.JointInstance.C0` and
      `Class.JointInstance.C1`.
      ##### Timing
      `Class.Motor6D` transforms are not applied immediately, unlike updating
      `Class.JointInstance.C0|C0` and `Class.JointInstance.C1|C1`, but rather as
      a batch in a parallel job after `Class.RunService.PreSimulation`,
      immediately before physics steps. The deferred batch update is much more
      efficient than many immediate updates.
      If the `Class.Motor6D` is part of an animated model with an
      `Class.Animator`, then `Class.Motor6D.Transform` will usually be
      overwritten every frame by the `Class.Animator` after
      `Class.RunService.PreAnimation` and before
      `Class.RunService.PreSimulation`.

  - name: Motor6D.Transform
    summary: |
      Describes the current animation offset of the `Class.Motor6D` joint.
    description: |
      The internal `Datatype.CFrame` that is manipulated when a `Class.Motor6D`
      is being animated. It is recommended to use this property for custom
      animations rather than `Class.JointInstance.C0` and
      `Class.JointInstance.C1`.
      ##### Timing
      `Class.Motor6D` transforms are not applied immediately, unlike updating
      `Class.JointInstance.C0|C0` and `Class.JointInstance.C1|C1`, but rather as
      a batch in a parallel job after `Class.RunService.PreSimulation`,
      immediately before physics steps. The deferred batch update is much more
      efficient than many immediate updates.
      If the `Class.Motor6D` is part of an animated model with an
      `Class.Animator`, then `Class.Motor6D.Transform` will usually be
      overwritten every frame by the `Class.Animator` after
      `Class.RunService.PreAnimation` and before
      `Class.RunService.PreSimulation`.

    type: CFrame
    tags:
      - Hidden
      - NotReplicated
    deprecation_message: ''
    security:

      write: None
    thread_safety: ReadSafe

## SetRoll
    summary: |
      Sets the current rotation applied around the camera's Z-axis.
    description: |
      This method is outdated and no longer considered best practice.
      This method sets the current roll, in radians, of the `Class.Camera`. The
      roll is applied after the `Class.Camera.CFrame|CFrame` and represents the
      rotation around the camera's Z-axis.
      For example, the following would invert the `Class.Camera`:
      ```lua
      workspace.CurrentCamera:SetRoll(math.pi) -- math.pi radians = 180 degrees
      ```
      SetRoll has no effect on any roll applied using the
      `Class.Camera.CFrame|CFrame` property. Roll applied using SetRoll is not
      reflected in the `Class.Camera.CFrame|CFrame` property but is reflected in
      the `Datatype.CFrame` returned
      by`Class.Camera:GetRenderCFrame()|GetRenderCFrame()`.
      This method can only be used when the `Class.Camera.CameraType|CameraType`
      is set to `Scriptable`, regardless of whether the default camera scripts
      are being used. If it is used with any other
      `Class.Camera.CameraType|CameraType` a warning is given in the output.
      Any roll applied using this method will be lost when the
      `Class.Camera.CameraType|CameraType` is changed from `Scriptable`.
      To obtain the roll set using this method use
      `Class.Camera:GetRoll()|GetRoll()`.
      As this method is outdated, you are advised to instead apply roll to the
      `Class.Camera` using the `Class.Camera.CFrame|CFrame` property. For
      example:
      ```lua
      local currentCFrame = workspace.CurrentCamera.CFrame
      local rollCFrame = CFrame.Angles(0, 0, roll)
## CameraType
    summary: |
      Specifies the `Enum.CameraType` to be read by the camera scripts.
    description: |
      The default Roblox camera scripts have several built-in behaviors. Setting
      this property toggles between the various `Enum.CameraType` behaviors.
      Note that some camera types require a valid
      `Class.Camera.CameraSubject|CameraSubject` to work correctly.
      The default camera scripts will not move or update the camera if
      `CameraType` is set to `Enum.CameraType.Scriptable`. For more information
      on positioning and orienting the camera manually, see
      `Class.Camera.CFrame|CFrame`.
      For all `CameraType` settings **except** `Enum.CameraType.Scriptable`, the
      `Class.Camera.CameraSubject|CameraSubject` property represents the object
      whose position the camera's `Class.Camera.Focus|Focus` is set to.
## CFrame
    summary: |
      The `Datatype.CFrame` of the `Class.Camera`, defining its position and
      orientation in the 3D world.
    description: |
      This property is the `Datatype.CFrame` of the `Class.Camera`, defining its
      position and orientation in the 3D world. Note that some transformations,
      such as the rotation of the head when using VR devices, are not reflected
      in this property, so you should use
      `Class.Camera:GetRenderCFrame()|GetRenderCFrame()` to obtain the "true"
      `Datatype.CFrame` of the camera.
      You can move the camera by setting this property. However, the default
      camera scripts also set it, so you should either:
      - Set the camera `Class.Camera.CameraType|CameraType` to
        `Enum.CameraType.Scriptable` so that the default camera scripts will not
        update the camera's `Datatype.CFrame`. This method is simplest and
        recommended in most cases.
      - Completely replace the default camera scripts with alternatives. This
        approach is only recommended if you do not need any default camera
        functionality.
      The most intuitive way to position and orient the `Class.Camera` is by
      using the `Datatype.CFrame.lookAt()` constructor. In the following
      example, the `Class.Camera` is positioned at
      `Datatype.Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)` and is oriented to be looking towards
      `Datatype.Vector3.new(10, 0, 0)`.
      ```lua
      local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
      camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable
      local pos = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
      local lookAtPos = Vector3.new(10, 0, 0)
      camera.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(pos, lookAtPos)
      ```
      Although the camera can be placed in the manner demonstrated above, you
      may want to animate it to move smoothly from one `Datatype.CFrame` to
      another. For this, you can either:
      - Set the camera's position/orientation every frame with
        `Class.RunService:BindToRenderStep()` and the `Datatype.CFrame:Lerp()`
        method.
      - Create and play a `Class.Tween` that animates the position/orientation
        of the camera:
        ```lua
## StepAnimations
    summary: |
      Increments the `Class.AnimationTrack.TimePosition` of all playing
      `Class.AnimationTrack|AnimationTracks` that are loaded onto the
      `Animator`, applying the offsets to the model associated with the
      `Animator`. For use in the command bar or by plugins only.
    description: |
      Increments the `Class.AnimationTrack.TimePosition` of all playing
      `Class.AnimationTrack|AnimationTracks` that are loaded onto the
      `Animator`, applying the offsets to the model associated with the
      `Animator`. For use in the command bar or by plugins only.
      The `deltaTime` parameter determines the number of seconds to increment on
      the animation's progress. Typically this method will be called in a loop
      to preview the length of an animation (see example).
      Note that once animations have stopped playing, the model's joints will
      need to be manually reset to their original positions (see example).
      #### Access
      This method requires Plugin-level security. It can only be called from the
      Studio command bar or from a `Class.Plugin`. Regular `Class.Script` and
      `Class.LocalScript` instances cannot call this method.
    code_samples:
      - Animator-StepAnimations
    parameters:
      - name: deltaTime
        type: float
        default:
        summary: |
          The amount of time in seconds animation playback is to be incremented.
          by.
    returns:
      - type: ()
        summary: ''
    tags: []
    deprecation_message: ''
    security: None
    thread_safety: Unsafe
    capabilities:
      - Animation
      - PluginOrOpenCloud

## StartVideoCaptureAsync
    summary: |
      Initiates a video capture recording.
    description: |
      This method initiates a video capture recording. The recording will
      continue until the
      `Class.CaptureService:StopVideoCapture()|StopVideoCapture()` method is
      called, or when 30 seconds have passed, whichever comes first. During the
      video recording, all user voices are muted.
      The `onCaptureReady` callback can be used to prompt the user to save or
      share the video capture.
      The `captureParams` parameter is currently non-operational.
    code_samples:
      - CaptureService-StartVideoCaptureAsync
    parameters:
      - name: onCaptureReady
        type: Function
        default:
        summary: |
          A callback function that is called on video capture completion with a
          `Enum.VideoCaptureResult` and, if successful, a `Class.VideoCapture`.
      - name: captureParams
        type: Dictionary
        default: nil
        summary: |
          A dictionary of optional parameters that modify capture behavior.
          Currently non-operational.
    returns:
      - type: VideoCaptureStartedResult
        summary: |
          A `Enum.VideoCaptureStartedResult` indicating whether the video
          recording started successfully.
    tags:
      - Yields
    deprecation_message: ''
    security: None
    thread_safety: Unsafe
    capabilities:
      - Capture

## Technology
    summary: |
      Determines the lighting system for rendering the 3D world. Non-scriptable.
    description: |
      Determines the lighting system for rendering the 3D world. This property
      is non‑scriptable and only modifiable in Studio.
    code_samples: []
    type: Technology
    tags:
      - Deprecated
    deprecation_message: |
      This property has been superseded by
      `Class.Lighting.LightingStyle|LightingStyle` which determines the artistic
      intent behind lighting, and
      `Class.Lighting.PrioritizeLightingQuality|PrioritizeLightingQuality` which
      indicates whether you prefer lighting/shading quality or view distance to
      scale down first.
    security:
      read: RobloxScriptSecurity
      write: RobloxScriptSecurity
    thread_safety: ReadSafe
    category: Appearance
    serialization:
      can_load: true
      can_save: true
    capabilities:
      - Environment
## LightingStyle
    summary: |
      The artistic intent behind lighting in the experience.
    description: |
      `LightingStyle` indicates the artistic intent behind lighting in the
      experience, as an `Enum.LightingStyle` option. `Enum.LightingStyle.Soft`
      is the stylized look; `Enum.LightingStyle.Realistic` is the naturalistic
      look. The actual shadowing path also depends on
      `Class.Lighting.PrioritizeLightingQuality|PrioritizeLightingQuality` (for
      example, Soft with that property enabled uses shadow maps rather than
      voxel lighting).
    type: LightingStyle
    tags: []
    deprecation_message: ''
    security:
      read: None
      write: None
    capabilities:
      - Environment
## PrioritizeLightingQuality
    summary: |
      Indicates whether you prefer lighting/shading quality or view distance to
      scale down first.
    description: |
      This property indicates whether you prefer lighting/shading quality or
      view distance to scale down first. As the rendering quality level reduces,
      a setting of `true` prioritizes features such as advanced shadows and
      high‑quality shaders at closer distances, while a setting of `false`
      prioritizes view distance.
    type: boolean
    tags: []
    deprecation_message: ''
    security:
      read: None
      write: None
    capabilities:
      - Environment

name: LightingStyle
summary: |
  Enum used by `Class.Lighting.LightingStyle` to indicate the artistic intent
  This enum indicates the artistic intent behind lighting in the experience. It
  - name: Realistic
    summary: |
      The most advanced and realistic lighting and shadows Roblox can deliver.
    value: 0
  - name: Soft
    summary: |
      A flat, retro-Roblox look with softer lights and shadows.
    value: 1
## Decal.Texture
    summary: |
      The content ID of the image to be applied by the `Class.Decal`.
    description: |
--
    type: ContentId
    tags: []
    deprecation_message: |
      This property has been deprecated. Use
      `Class.Decal.ColorMapContent|ColorMapContent` for future work.
    security:
## Decal.ColorMap
    summary: |
      Content ID that determines the color and opacity of the surface.
    description: |
      This property takes a content ID to determine the color and opacity of the
      surface. This texture is sometimes called the **albedo** texture.
    code_samples: []
    type: ContentId
    tags:
      - NotReplicated
    deprecation_message: ''
    security:
      read: None
## HD.Face
    summary: |
      Determines the asset ID of the Face to be applied to the `Class.Humanoid`.
    description: |
      **Face** determines the asset ID of the Face to be
--
    type: int64
    tags: []
    deprecation_message: ''
    security:
      read: None
      write: None
## SetAccessories
    summary: |
      Accepts a table that sets the accessories and related properties for an
      avatar.
    description: |
      Accepts a table that sets the accessories and related properties for an
      avatar. If the second parameter (includeRigidAccessories) is true, then
      this function can also be used to set the rigid accessories in the rigid
      accessory properties. In this case any table entry that does not have an
      Order will be considered a rigid accessory and put in the appropriate
      property according to the AccessoryType.
    code_samples:
      - set-accessories
    parameters:
      - name: accessories
        type: Array
        default:
        summary: |
          Each entry specifies for an individual accessory the AccessoryType,
          AssetId, IsLayered, Order and Puffiness.
      - name: includeRigidAccessories
        type: boolean
        default:
        summary: |
          Set to true if rigid accessories are also included in the passed in
          array (they would have to not specify Order).
    returns:
      - type: ()
        summary: ''
    tags: []
    deprecation_message: ''
    security: None
    thread_safety: Unsafe
    capabilities:
      - AvatarAppearance

6:Almost everything in Roblox is represented as a cloud-based asset with a unique corresponding ID. This ID is typically in the form of `rbxassetid://[ID]`, which gets applied to various instances as a property that's appropriate for that particular asset type. For example, `Class.Texture`, `Class.MeshPart`, and `Class.AudioPlayer` instances reference image, mesh, and audio assets through their respective `Class.Text 10: `rbxassetid://7229442422` 14: `rbxassetid://6768917255` 18: `rbxassetid://9125402735` 25:When you import assets, they must pass a [moderation](#asset-moderation) check before users can see and interact with them in published games. After Roblox approves imported assets, you can choose to retain ownership of their usage on the platform or make them publicly available as detailed in [Asset permissions](#asset-permissions). 115:### rbxassetid 117:`rbxassetid` points to a user-uploaded asset on Roblox. This format is a common standard for properties such as `Class.Decal.ColorMapContent`, `Class.ParticleEmitter.Texture`, and `Class.AudioPlayer.Asset`. 121: 126: 131: 156:### rbxthumb 158:`rbxthumb` points to a thumbnail image for the provided asset. Its string format takes a thumbnail type (`type`), an asset ID (`id`), and width/height (`w`/`h`). 160:
273:`rbxgameasset` only works for the current game. If you paste a parent object that utilizes the asset into another game, the asset will not load (or will load a different asset if you've uploaded one with the same name to that other game). If you need an asset to work across multiple games, use `rbxassetid` instead of `rbxgameasset`. 294:## Asset permissions 296:An asset's privacy status determines who has permission to use the asset within their games. By default, all assets are **private** when you or your [group](../../projects/groups.md) members import them into Studio. If you want to grant everyone access to the asset ID, you must distribute the asset to the [Creator Store][CreatorMarketplaceURL]. 299:Special privacy rules and workflows apply to **audio** and **video** assets. See [asset privacy](../../projects/assets/privacy.md) for details on sharing these asset types among friends and games. 302:## Asset moderation 304:Roblox performs both human and automated asset moderation on a proactive and reactive basis to ensure assets adhere to the [Community Rules](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/articles/203313410), [Terms of Use](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/articles/115004647846), and [Intellectual Property guidelines](../../production/publishing/ip-guidelines.md). If any asset violates these moderation policies, such as including di 306:If an asset is still in the moderation queue when you publish your game, users cannot see or interact with the asset until Roblox approves it. If the asset doesn't pass moderation, you will receive a [notification](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/360020870412-Understanding-Moderation-Messages) explaining why the asset cannot be on the platform in its current state. content.content:
name: import-asset
description: Import a 3D model from an external modelling program (Blender, Maya, 3ds Max, Cinema 4D, Houdini, SketchUp, or any tool that exports glTF/GLB or FBX) into the open Studio place by exporting it, uploading it through Open Cloud with open_cloud_invoke, inserting it, and verifying that geometry, textures, colours, scale, orientation, anchoring, and placement survived. Use whenever the user asks to bring, move, import, send, or copy a model, scene, or mesh from another program or a local model file into Studio. MCP clients only.
# Importing a Model from an External Program
Four stages: **export 
 upload 
 insert 
 verify and repair**. The importer regularly changes scale, rotation, colours and sometimes textures on the way in, so **verifying is required**.
Read `rbx-open-cloud-usage` (how `open_cloud_invoke` works) and `rbx-permissions` (checking and asking for permissions) first. Never work around a permission error.
## Tool call notes
- `execute_luau` needs `datamodel_type: "Edit"` for everything in this skill.
- `screen_capture` needs a `capture_id`.
- The `skill` tool takes `skill_name`.
- End each `execute_luau` edit with `game:GetService("ChangeHistoryService"):SetWaypoint("<description>")`.
## 0. Settle the up-front questions
Uploads create **permanent assets**: Open Cloud can't archive or delete Model or Image assets; only the Creator Dashboard can.
**Permissions needed:** **Publish & manage assets 
 `asset:write` and `asset:read`**, plus an approved upload folder. Probe the scopes first:
open_cloud_invoke(method: "GET", endpoint: "/cloud/v2/universes/<game.GameId>", scopes: ["asset:read", "asset:write"])
Ask once, together, for whatever you don't already know:
- **Any missing scope**, named by section and toggle.
- **The upload folder** approved in MCP Permissions (no tool lists them). Write exports straight into it.
- **Consent to create assets**, saying whose account they'll go on.
- **A supplied file outside an approved folder:** ask the user to approve its folder or move the file there themselves. Don't copy or move it yourself.
Reuse anything the user already told you. Ask detail-reduction questions when step 2 finds the need. Upload only what's needed, and reuse asset IDs you already have.
## 1. Gather context
1. Call `list_roblox_studios`, then use the instance the user means. Studio instance IDs change when a place is reopened; if a call says the ID is not connected, list again.
2. Find the creator:
   ```lua
   return { creatorType = tostring(game.CreatorType), creatorId = game.CreatorId,
            userId = game:GetService("StudioService"):GetUserId() }
   ```
   For `Enum.CreatorType.Group`, upload with `creationContext.creator.groupId` = `creatorId`. Otherwise upload with `userId`.
## 2. Inspect and export from the source program
How you reach the source program depends on what you have:
- **The program has a tool or MCP integration you can drive:** inspect the scene and run the export yourself.
- **You can't drive the program:** ask the user to export the file with the settings below into an approved directory, and to tell you the path.
73303: Studio itself must also be visible on the monitor: if it is occluded or minimized, the capture will return whatever is on screen at the widget/window's position instead of the plugin GUI.
75748:5. If the subject is not in frame, say so plainly ('not visible in this view'). A question mentioning X is NOT evidence that X is present - do not be led by it.

# Findings (researched 2026-11-13)

Quotes came through a fetch-and-summarize tool, so check exact wording against the pages before publishing. "Staff" is inferred from post content, since the pages show no badges.

## 1. Several Studio windows on one PC

- **Official statement that multi-window is supported: not found** in create.roblox.com docs or the help center. The only official acknowledgement is indirect, through the MCP posts below.
- **[official, staff post, 2026-03-05]** Multiple running Studio instances are an assumed scenario: "A single MCP client can now connect to multiple running Studio instances" (marked experimental). https://devforum.roblox.com/t/assistant-updates-studio-built-in-mcp-server-and-playtest-automation/4474643
- **[community report, 2026-08-18, unresolved]** Opening a new window (File > Open from File, Open from Roblox, or relaunching Studio) closes the existing one for this reporter, who recalls running up to five instances before. Staff reply 2026-08-24: "We cannot reproduce this issue." https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studio-closes-existing-window-when-opening-a-new-one/4817979
- **[community report, 2025-06-05]** A memory-based window limit exists: "You've reached the limit for open Studio window. Please close some to free up memory." The reporter said it cleared itself by 2025-06-07. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/latest-studio-update-doesnt-allow-multiple-windows-open-at-the-same-time/3679128
- **[community report, older, not opened]** Search results list a thread on local and published places not opening together (https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studio-not-allowing-local-place-files-and-published-place-files-to-be-opened-at-the-same-time/1154915) and one on crashes beyond 3 windows (https://devforum.roblox.com/t/new-studio-windows-crash-beyond-3-open-windows/82193).
- **Same place opened twice, Team Create limits, memory per instance, login session: not found.**

## 2. Built-in Studio MCP: multiple instances and clients

- **[community bug report, 2026-07-10, open, no staff reply]** Thread 4729586: when a Studio window opens while `StudioMCP.exe` is already running, `list_roblox_studios` returns an empty list with "The previously active Studio instance has disconnected."
  - Environment: Studio 0.729.0.7290838, Windows 11. The reporter blames the new `RBX_STUDIO_NS-{PID}` named pipe not being discovered.
  - Workaround: open the MCP panel widget inside Studio.

Quotes from DevForum, about.roblox.com and OBS pages came back from the fetch tool as short fragments, so they are exact but partial.

## PART 1: Roblox rules

- **Name and Logo Guidelines** (a). Now titled "Roblox Name and Logo Guidelines", last edited 2026-11-01. https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001708126
  - **Videos:** it contains no sentence about YouTube, videos, channel names or disclaimers.
  - **Logo:** "Besides our official badge, we do not permit the general use of our logo in any creative or copy."
  - **Logo, second statement:** "Logo use is strictly limited to select partners and the Roblox Stars Influencer Program."
  - **Avatars and commercial use:** "The use of the Roblox name (and any name similar to Roblox), badge, logo, and other trademarks and copyrights including “Classic Roblox Avatars” (R6 and R15 avatars, as defined below*) is not permitted on physical products or commercial content and may not be tied to the development, distribution or sale of any products or services (including, but not limited to, physical products, packaging, retail displays, services, NFTs, film, TV, books, stage shows or amusement parks) without a Roblox licensing agreement."
  - **Don'ts:** "Imply official Roblox partnership or endorsement."
  - **Names:** the "Roblox"/"Blox" ban covers Game titles, Creator user names, display names and Group/Community names on the platform. It does not mention YouTube channels.

- **DevForum "Update to Roblox Licensing Program & Brand Guidelines"** (a: Roblox staff post signed "Developer Relations", 2022-06-23). https://devforum.roblox.com/t/update-to-roblox-licensing-program-brand-guidelines/1843674
  - **Question:** "Do the new IP usage guidelines restrict me from creating videos or streaming content using the R6 or R15 avatars?"
  - **Answer fragments:** "No, the Guidelines do not restrict this." / "You are free to continue using all avatar types in your social media content and you may continue monetizing that content" / "(such as through YouTube ad revenue)."
  - **Disclaimer:** "if your channel or fan site uses “Roblox” or “Blox,” please make sure you say that your page is not affiliated with Roblox."
  - **Exception (paraphrase):** a TV show or movie with classic R6/R15 avatars requires contacting Roblox.
  - **Caveat:** this 2022 FAQ is the only explicit permission for monetized videos I found. The 2026 guideline text bans "commercial content" without carving out videos, so the report should cite both.

- **Terms of Use** (a). Effective date 2026-11-01. https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846-Roblox-Terms-of-Use
  - **No video licence:** a text search of the full article finds no clause on recording, streaming, machinima, YouTube or ad revenue.
  - **3.4.1 Prohibited uses:** "Roblox-Owned Content may not be used outside of the Services unless such use is both (a) expressly authorized by Roblox; and (b) consistent with Roblox's Name and Logo Guidelines."
  - **3.4 definition:** Roblox-Owned Content includes "trademarks, avatar models, clothing items, Roblox-published Games".
  - **Trademarks:** "Use by you of any Roblox trademarks outside of the Services (including a trademark that may be contained in the title of a Game) is permitted only as set forth in the Roblox Name and Logo Guidelines."
  - **Other creators' UGC:** "Any acquisition of UGC on the Services is solely for your personal entertainment."
  - **No off-platform grant:** I found no clause granting users rights to use other creators' Marketplace or Creator Store items in off-platform video (c: no explicit permission or prohibition specific to video).

- **Audio** (a). Same Terms of Use, Creator Terms 7.1 "Licensed Music".
  - **Licence scope:** "Roblox grants you: (a) a non-exclusive, personal, limited, revocable, non-transferable license only to synchronize Licensed Music into a Game or other Content solely on the Services and only during the period when Roblox makes such Licensed Music available"
  - **Prohibition:** you will not "export, extract, download, or provide a way for anyone else to export, extract, or download the Licensed Music for use anywhere outside of the Services."
  - **Practical reading:** do not put Roblox catalog music or sound effects in the YouTube audio track; use separately licensed audio.

- **Community Standards** (a). The help article now only redirects to https://about.roblox.com/community-standards
  - **Romantic and Sexual Content:** "Roblox isn't the place for seeking offline or online romantic connections or engaging with sexual content or behavior"
  - **Intellectual property:** Roblox "will remove infringing content upon receiving a valid copyright or trademark takedown request from a rights holder"
  - **Off-platform:** a "Harmful Off-Platform Speech or Behavior" section exists.

## PART 2: Recording

- **Studio built-in recorder** (c for official docs). I found no create.roblox.com page documenting a Studio "Record Video" feature, format or resolution.
  - (b) A July 2025 thread says "When pressing F12 in Studio, red lines normally appear around the window to indicate a recording is being made", and reports it fails in a "run" session. A later addition mentions an MP4 file with audio only. No staff reply. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/unable-to-record-studio-in-run-session-using-f12/3850174
  - (b) Older threads complain of WMV output, reduced resolution and dropped frames. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/the-recording-tools-need-to-be-upgraded-urgently/2823204
  - (a) A Roblox staff guide (2024-02-13) recommends OBS for Studio video and mentions no built-in recorder. Its tips: Editor Quality 21, "Set Graphics Quality to its maximum level", and "L CTRL + L SHIFT + C to toggle basic UI visibility" in free camera. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/tips-for-capturing-high-quality-screenshots-and-videos-in-studio/2723897
  - Whether the F12 recorder still exists in 2026 Studio: (c).

- **CaptureService** (a). https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/CaptureService and the source YAML at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/reference/engine/classes/CaptureService.yaml
  - **Video API exists:** `StartVideoCaptureAsync(onCaptureReady, captureParams)` and `StopVideoCapture()`. The class is described as "a client-side service".
  - **Limit:** the YAML says recording runs until `StopVideoCapture()` or 30 seconds (paraphrase). The announcement says "Each recording can only last for a maximum of 30 seconds." https://devforum.roblox.com/t/beta-video-captures-api-bring-your-gameplay-moments-to-life/3823116 (2025-07-18)
  - **Parameters:** "The `captureParams` parameter is currently non-operational."
  - **Storage:** "The capture is not immediately saved to the user's capture gallery." The user must be prompted via `PromptSaveCapturesToGallery`.
  - **In-experience capture article:** "Videos are saved to your Roblox app storage", exportable to "the "Videos" folder on desktop". It also says "audio from voice chat or other in-experience sounds are not recorded" and that in-experience UI is removed. https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/203314190
  - **Works in Studio, resolution, format:** not stated anywhere official (c).
  - **Practical reading:** unsuitable for Shorts production (30 s cap, no audio, manual save).

- **Offline or frame-by-frame rendering.**
  - (a) The built-in Studio MCP server has a `screen_capture` tool: "Captures the current Studio viewport and returns the image data." It is stills only; no video tool is listed. https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/mcp
  - (a) The older `Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server` is "no longer being actively developed" and has no capture tool. https://github.com/Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server
  - (b) Moon Animator exports rigs and KeyframeSequences, not video; forum advice is to screen-record. https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-record-trailers-with-moon-animation-suite/1923201
  - (c) I found no official or reliable offline video renderer and no evidence for ViewportFrame-based export. Stepping frames with `screen_capture` is my inference, untested.

- **OBS capture source** (a).
  - Game Capture "is the most efficient way you can add your games to OBS Studio and should always be tried first." It "directly captures the DirectX or OpenGL game", and "This is not suitable for non-game window capture." https://obsproject.com/kb/game-capture-source
  - Window Capture methods are Automatic (default), BitBlt and Windows 10: "BitBlt is less efficient but may help with certain programs." https://obsproject.com/kb/window-capture-sources
  - Which source works with Roblox Studio specifically: (c), no official statement; test Game Capture in "Capture specific window" mode first, then Window Capture.

- **OBS encoder settings** (a). https://obsproject.com/kb/advanced-recording-settings-guide
  - NVENC: "Rate Control: Constant QP", "Constant QP: 16-23", "Keyframe Interval: 2", "Preset: P5".
  - x264: "Rate Control: CRF", "CRF: 16-23", "CPU Usage Preset: veryfast".
  - AMD: "Rate Control: CQP", "CQ Level: 16-23", "Preset: Quality".
  - Intel: "Rate Control: ICQ", "ICQ Quality: 16-23", "Target Usage: TU4".

- **OBS container** (a).
  - "MKV is recommended in case of unforeseen issues arising." Remux via File > Remux Recordings. https://obsproject.com/kb/standard-recording-output-guide
  - "Hybrid MP4 and Hybrid MOV are the names of new output formats introduced in OBS 30.2 (Hybrid MP4)"; it stays recoverable after a crash. https://obsproject.com/kb/hybrid-mp4

- **OBS canvas, output resolution and FPS** (c). I found no knowledge base article that covers Base/Output resolution, typing a custom 1080x1920 canvas, or the FPS setting; the guessed URLs returned 404. The aspect-ratio guide only says non-16:9 is valid "if you are targeting a specific platform that is optimized for other aspect ratios." https://obsproject.com/kb/aspect-ratio-guide

- **OBS automation** (a).
  - "obs-websocket is now included by default with OBS Studio 28.0.0 and above."; the server runs "by default on port 4455". Settings are under Tools > "obs-websocket Settings". https://github.com/obsproject/obs-websocket
  - `StartRecord`: "Starts the record output." `StopRecord`: "Stops the record output.", returning `outputPath` ("File name for the saved recording"). `GetRecordStatus` returns `outputActive`, `outputTimecode` and `outputDuration`. All "Added in v5.0.0". https://github.com/obsproject/obs-websocket/blob/master/docs/generated/protocol.md
  - Confirmed also at https://obsproject.com/kb/remote-control-guide

## PART 3: Studio system requirements

- (a) https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/setup and the include file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/includes/studio/system-reqs.md agree. The table has only three rows:
  - **OS Version:** minimum "Windows 10" / "macOS 10.14"; recommended "Windows 11" / "macOS 14+".
  - **Memory (RAM):** minimum "3 GB"; recommended "8 GB".
  - **Resolution:** minimum blank; recommended "1600×900 or higher".
- The current official table lists no GPU, CPU, storage or internet requirement.

  - Which source works with Roblox Studio specifically: (c), no official statement; test Game Capture in "Capture specific window" mode first, then Window Capture.

- **OBS encoder settings** (a). https://obsproject.com/kb/advanced-recording-settings-guide
  - NVENC: "Rate Control: Constant QP", "Constant QP: 16-23", "Keyframe Interval: 2", "Preset: P5".
  - x264: "Rate Control: CRF", "CRF: 16-23", "CPU Usage Preset: veryfast".
  - AMD: "Rate Control: CQP", "CQ Level: 16-23", "Preset: Quality".
  - Intel: "Rate Control: ICQ", "ICQ Quality: 16-23", "Target Usage: TU4".

- **OBS container** (a).
  - "MKV is recommended in case of unforeseen issues arising." Remux via File > Remux Recordings. https://obsproject.com/kb/standard-recording-output-guide
  - "Hybrid MP4 and Hybrid MOV are the names of new output formats introduced in OBS 30.2 (Hybrid MP4)"; it stays recoverable after a crash. https://obsproject.com/kb/hybrid-mp4

- **OBS canvas, output resolution and FPS** (c). I found no knowledge base article that covers Base/Output resolution, typing a custom 1080x1920 canvas, or the FPS setting; the guessed URLs returned 404. The aspect-ratio guide only says non-16:9 is valid "if you are targeting a specific platform that is optimized for other aspect ratios." https://obsproject.com/kb/aspect-ratio-guide

- **OBS automation** (a).
  - "obs-websocket is now included by default with OBS Studio 28.0.0 and above."; the server runs "by default on port 4455". Settings are under Tools > "obs-websocket Settings". https://github.com/obsproject/obs-websocket
  - `StartRecord`: "Starts the record output." `StopRecord`: "Stops the record output.", returning `outputPath` ("File name for the saved recording"). `GetRecordStatus` returns `outputActive`, `outputTimecode` and `outputDuration`. All "Added in v5.0.0". https://github.com/obsproject/obs-websocket/blob/master/docs/generated/protocol.md
  - Confirmed also at https://obsproject.com/kb/remote-control-guide

## PART 3: Studio system requirements

- (a) https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/setup and the include file https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/includes/studio/system-reqs.md agree. The table has only three rows:
  - **OS Version:** minimum "Windows 10" / "macOS 10.14"; recommended "Windows 11" / "macOS 14+".
  - **Memory (RAM):** minimum "3 GB"; recommended "8 GB".
  - **Resolution:** minimum blank; recommended "1600×900 or higher".
- The current official table lists no GPU, CPU, storage or internet requirement.
- Help-center Studio requirements article: not fetched (c).</result>

# Roblox Studio por MCP y trabajo en paralelo: informe técnico

Fecha de la investigación: 2026-11-13. Versión de Studio analizada: 0.747.0.7471481
(`version-63eb6055af4e4688`), `StudioMCP.exe` 1.0.0 (362829b).

## Cómo leer este informe

Cada afirmación lleva una de estas etiquetas:

- **[OFICIAL]**: confirmado en documentación oficial de Roblox, OBS o Anthropic, o en una
  publicación firmada por personal de Roblox en DevForum.
- **[BINARIO]**: leído directamente en los archivos de Studio 0.747 (cadenas de texto de
  `StudioMCP.exe` y del plugin integrado `Assistant.rbxm`, y la salida de
  `StudioMCP.exe --help`). Es un hecho sobre esta versión, pero no está documentado y puede
  cambiar o estar apagado por una bandera remota.
- **[COMUNIDAD]**: reportado por usuarios en DevForum o GitHub, sin confirmación oficial.
- **[INFERENCIA]**: deducción mía a partir de lo anterior. No está probado.

Nada de este informe se probó contra un Studio en ejecución, porque en este equipo Studio
no abre. Todo lo marcado como inferencia, y también lo marcado como binario, debe
comprobarse en el equipo de casa antes de darlo por cierto. La sección 9 trae la lista de
comprobaciones.

### Hallazgo previo: Studio ya no está instalado en este equipo

La tarea partía de que `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\Versions\version-63eb6055af4e4688` contenía
`StudioMCP.exe`. Hoy esa carpeta solo contiene `RobloxStudioInstaller.exe`. El registro
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\logs\RobloxStudioInstaller_68C81.log` muestra que a las 07:07 (hora
local) el instalador corrió en modo `Uninstall` y borró `RobloxStudioBeta.exe` y el resto.
No lo reinstalé ni intenté abrir Studio.

Para poder inspeccionar los binarios descargué a una carpeta temporal los paquetes públicos
de esa misma versión desde el servidor de instalación de Roblox
(`https://setup.rbxcdn.com/version-63eb6055af4e4688-RobloxStudio.zip` y
`...-BuiltInStandalonePlugins.zip`), extraje `StudioMCP.exe` (SHA-256
`023162f8689a3ef6043387269fe0ccc6a9eca0fc55afd6567dbb3cc567cec7aa`) y
`Assistant.rbxm`, y busqué cadenas de texto. Solo ejecuté `StudioMCP.exe --help` y
`--version`, que no lanzan Studio.

`mcp.bat` no viene en ningún paquete de instalación y no existe en este equipo: lo genera
Studio cuando llega a ejecutarse **[INFERENCIA]**. Por eso su contenido no se pudo leer.

---

## 1. Servidor MCP integrado de Studio

### 1.1 Arquitectura

- **[OFICIAL]** El servidor viene dentro de Studio, corre como proceso local y habla con el
  cliente por transporte `stdio`
  ([doc oficial](https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/mcp),
  [fuente en GitHub](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Roblox/creator-docs/main/content/en-us/studio/mcp.md),
  última actualización del archivo: 2026-11-12).
- **[BINARIO]** `StudioMCP.exe` se describe a sí mismo como "MCP proxy for Roblox Studio".
  Sus únicas opciones son `-v/--verbose`, `-s/--stdio` ("No-opt for now"), `-h` y `-V`.
- **[BINARIO]** Funciona en tres capas:
  1. Cada cliente MCP (cada sesión de Claude Code) lanza **su propio** proceso
     `StudioMCP.exe` por stdio.
  2. El primer `StudioMCP.exe` que arranca abre un servidor WebSocket local ("WS host") en
     el puerto **13469** de `localhost`, con las rutas `/studio`, `/proxy`, `/health` y
     `/capture`. Los `StudioMCP.exe` siguientes encuentran el puerto ocupado ("Port already
     in use ... this process is not the host") y se conectan al primero como "proxy" por
     `ws://127.0.0.1:13469/proxy`.
  3. Cada ventana de Studio con el MCP activado se conecta a `ws://localhost:13469/studio`
     y se registra con un identificador.
  El host enruta cada petición al Studio indicado por `studio_id` y devuelve la respuesta
  al proxy que la pidió ("Routing request from proxy ... to studio ...", "Forwarding
  response ... to proxy ...").
- **[BINARIO]** Si el proceso host muere, los demás intentan tomar el puerto ("WS host
  server exited, will try to re-bind", "Reconnecting in ..."). Hay un token de
  autenticación guardado en la carpeta de datos de Roblox
  (`FFlagStudioMCPProxyTokenEnforce`, "Rejected WebSocket request: mode=enforce ...
  status=401") y se rechazan peticiones con cabecera `Origin` de navegador.
- **[COMUNIDAD]** Ese control de token causó un fallo temporal: desde el 2026-10-27 hubo
  reportes de Studio recibiendo 401 de StudioMCP
  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studio-mcp-studio-always-gets-401-unauthorized-from-studiomcp-token-enforcement-on-studio-never-passes/4960526)).

### 1.2 Activación y conexión de Claude Code

- **[OFICIAL]** Activar: abrir Assistant, menú "...", Manage MCP Servers, encender "Enable
  Studio as MCP server". Con un cliente conectado aparece un indicador verde con el número
  de clientes.
- **[OFICIAL]** Conexión rápida (Quick connect): Assistant Settings, MCP Servers,
  desplegable Quick connect, encender "Claude Code". Clientes soportados: Antigravity,
  Codex CLI, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Gemini CLI y Visual Studio Code.
- **[OFICIAL]** Comando manual en Windows: `cmd.exe /c %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat`.
  Configuración JSON equivalente:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "Roblox_Studio": {
      "command": "cmd.exe",
      "args": ["/c", "%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Roblox\\mcp.bat"]
    }
  }
}
```

- **[BINARIO]** El plugin de Assistant arma para Claude Code exactamente esta plantilla:
  `claude mcp add --transport stdio Roblox_Studio -- <comando>`. Con el comando oficial de
  Windows queda:

```
claude mcp add --transport stdio --scope user Roblox_Studio -- cmd.exe /c %LOCALAPPDATA%\Roblox\mcp.bat
```

  El `--scope user` lo agrego yo para que sirva en todas las carpetas de proyecto; la
  plantilla del plugin no trae alcance. Esto confirma el comando que `docs/03` daba como
  "sin verificar", aunque sigue sin probarse en vivo.
- **[BINARIO]** Quick connect busca y edita `~/.claude.json` (o
  `%CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR%\.claude.json`) y también lee `~/.claude/settings.json`. Antes de
  modificar deja una copia con sufijo `.roblox-studio-backup`. En el mismo módulo hay
  código que agrega ganchos (`UserPromptSubmit`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`) a la
  configuración de Claude Code, ligado a un ajuste llamado "Data access" cuyo texto es: "To
  help improve the Studio experience, provide Roblox with access to prompt information. You
  can change this setting at any time." **[INFERENCIA]** Si ese ajuste queda encendido,
  Studio puede instalar un gancho que comparte con Roblox información de tus prompts.
  Revisa ese interruptor y el contenido de `~/.claude/settings.json` después de usar Quick
  connect. Si prefieres control total, usa el comando manual.
- **[OFICIAL]** Alcances de Claude Code
  ([doc de Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)): `local` (por defecto, en
  `~/.claude.json`, solo el proyecto actual), `project` (archivo `.mcp.json` en la raíz del
  proyecto, pensado para compartir) y `user` (en `~/.claude.json`, todos los proyectos).
  `.mcp.json` admite expansión `${VAR}` y `${VAR:-valor}`. Sintaxis:
  `claude mcp add [opciones] <nombre> -- <comando> [args...]`.
- **[COMUNIDAD]** `mcp.bat` falla si la ruta del perfil de Windows tiene un espacio (por
  ejemplo un nombre de usuario con espacio); la salida es apuntar el cliente directo a
  `StudioMCP.exe`
  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/mcpbat-fails-to-launch-studio-mcp-due-to-unquoted-path-containing-spaces-roblox-is-not-recognized/4975979)).
  **[INFERENCIA]** Apuntar directo a `StudioMCP.exe` tiene un costo: vive en
  `Versions\version-XXXX\`, y esa carpeta cambia con cada actualización de Studio, así que
  habría que corregir la ruta cada semana. En el equipo de casa conviene un usuario de
  Windows sin espacios y usar `mcp.bat`.
- **[OFICIAL]** Después de que Studio se actualiza hay que reiniciar una vez el cliente de
  IA ([DevForum, personal de Roblox, 2026-08-19](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studio-mcp-multi-agent-improvements-and-connected-ai-clients/4820583)).

### 1.3 Lista de herramientas

**[OFICIAL]** Lista publicada en la doc al 2026-11-12. "Every tool call takes a `studio_id`
parameter that names the Studio instance it targets."

| Grupo | Herramienta | Qué hace y parámetros conocidos |
|---|---|---|
| Sesión | `list_roblox_studios` | Lista las instancias conectadas. **[BINARIO]** Cada resultado trae `id`, `name` (incluye el id del lugar o el nombre del archivo), `mode` (`Edit`/`Play`), `state`, y `persistedToCloud`, `placeId`, `universeId` o `file` según cómo esté guardado el lugar. |
| Luau | `execute_luau` | Ejecuta Luau y devuelve el resultado o el error. Requiere `datamodel_type`: `Edit`, `Client` o `Server`. |
| Scripts | `script_read` | Lee un script por ruta con puntos (`game.ServerScriptService.MyScript`), completo o por rango de líneas. |
| Scripts | `multi_edit` | Aplica varias ediciones a un script; si la ruta no existe, **crea el script**. Requiere `datamodel_type` (Edit). **[BINARIO]** Forma: `{"file_path":"ReplicatedStorage.X","edits":[{"old_string":"...","new_string":"..."}]}`. |
| Scripts | `script_search` | Búsqueda difusa por nombre de script, máximo 10 resultados. |
| Scripts | `script_grep` | Busca un patrón en todos los scripts, máximo 50 coincidencias. |
| Explorar | `search_game_tree` | Árbol de instancias en JSON plano. **[BINARIO]** Parámetros: `datamodel_type`, `path`, `instance_type`, `keywords`, `max_depth`, `head_limit`. |
| Explorar | `inspect_instance` | Propiedades, atributos y resumen de hijos de una instancia. |
| Explorar | `subagent` | Lanza un subagente interno de tipo `explore` o `playtest`. |
| Prueba | `get_studio_state` | Estado de Studio: si está en juego y qué `datamodel_type` hay disponibles. |
| Prueba | `start_stop_play` | Inicia o detiene la prueba. **[BINARIO]** Parámetro `is_start` (booleano): "true to start the game, false to stop the game and return to edit mode". |
| Prueba | `get_console_output` | Devuelve la salida de la ventana Output. |
| Prueba | `screen_capture` | Captura el visor y devuelve la imagen. **[BINARIO]** `capture_id` (texto, obligatorio), y opcionales `camera_position` y `look_at_position` (arreglos de 3 números, deben ir juntos). Descripción interna: "Capture current edit-time screen". |
| Entrada | `character_navigation` | Mueve al personaje del jugador a una posición o instancia. |
| Entrada | `user_keyboard_input` | Secuencia de teclas: keyDown, keyUp, keyPress, textInput, wait. |
| Entrada | `user_mouse_input` | Secuencia de ratón: mover, clic, botón, rueda, wait (0 a 10000 ms). |
| Recursos | `search_asset` | Busca en Creator Store y en el inventario del creador. |
| Recursos | `insert_asset` | Inserta un recurso por su id numérico (modelos, mallas, imágenes, audio, video, animaciones, paquetes). |
| Recursos | `upload_image` | "Uploads a batch of images from HTTP URLs to the Roblox asset server, returning an image path to asset ID map." **[BINARIO]** Recibe un arreglo de rutas HTTP; el ejemplo interno es `{"http://localhost/image.png": "rbxassetid://12345678"}`. |
| Recursos | `store_image` | Carga una imagen **local** y devuelve un URI `IMAGEID_<id>` para pasarlo a otras herramientas de generación. **No sube nada a Roblox.** **[BINARIO]** Solo png, jpg, jpeg; máximo 5 MB; ruta absoluta. |
| Generación | `generate_mesh`, `generate_material`, `generate_procedural_model`, `wait_job_finished` | Malla con textura, variante de material, modelo procedural de piezas primitivas y espera del trabajo. |
| Generación | `generate_animation` | Animación **R15** desde texto, o convierte una animación R6 existente a R15; hasta 10 segundos. |
| Docs | `http_get` | Lee URLs permitidas de la documentación de Roblox. |
| Docs | `skill` | Carga guías internas (por ejemplo `rbx-open-cloud-usage`, `rbx-permissions`, `rbx-import-asset`). |
| Lugar | `save_place` | Guarda como Archivo, Guardar; sin diálogos. **[BINARIO]** Devuelve `Saved`, `NotNeeded`, `NeedsUserAction` (lugar nunca guardado: necesita Guardar como a mano una vez), `Busy` (hay una prueba en curso) o `Failed`. Nunca publica. |
| Open Cloud | `open_cloud_invoke` | Llama APIs de Open Cloud sin llave. Parámetros `method`, `endpoint`, `body`, `scopes`, `files`. Solo en lugares de un juego publicado ([doc oficial](https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/mcp-open-cloud)). |
| Otros | `submit_feedback` | Envía comentarios a Roblox sobre las herramientas. |

**[BINARIO]** Nombres de herramientas que existen en el plugin de esta versión pero **no**
están en la doc pública. Pueden ser internas de Assistant o estar apagadas por bandera; la
única forma de saber si tu Studio las expone es mirar la lista real (`/mcp` en Claude
Code):

- `video_capture`: "Start or stop recording a video of the game." Parámetro `is_start`.
  Al detener devuelve JSON con `recording_id`, `status` (`completed` o `partial`; "partial"
  indica que la captura terminó antes, "for example the duration limit") y rutas de
  archivos (`video`, `manifest`, `frame_times`). Controlada por
  `FFlagAssistantMCPVideoCapture`. Es relevante para la sección 5.
- `list_place`, `open_place`, `close_place`: listar y abrir lugares desde la página de
  inicio (`FFlagAssistantMcpListPlaceTool`).
- `generate_texture`, `generate_scene`, `generate_avatar`, `auto_setup_avatar`,
  `segment_mesh`, `capture_plugin_gui`, `list_plugin_guis`, `list_skills`,
  `cloud_execute_luau`.
- `set_active_studio` todavía aparece en textos de guías viejas dentro del plugin, pero
  fue retirada (ver sección 2).

### 1.4 Límites conocidos

**Contexto de ejecución**

- **[OFICIAL]** `execute_luau` exige `datamodel_type`: `Edit`, `Client` o `Server`.
- **[BINARIO]** "use "Edit" in edit mode, or "Client"/"Server" during a playtest. "Edit"
  is rejected while playing".
- **[OFICIAL]** "Play mode takes over Studio": durante una prueba fallan las herramientas
  que apuntan al modelo de edición
  ([personal de Roblox, 2026-08-19](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studio-mcp-multi-agent-improvements-and-connected-ai-clients/4820583)).

**Tiempo de ejecución**

- **[BINARIO]** No hay un tiempo máximo declarado. La descripción de la herramienta dice:
  "Code runs on Studio's main thread; until it yields, Studio is frozen, the script can't
  be stopped, and the MCP connection may drop." Recomienda partir el trabajo pesado en
  tandas (unos 1000 elementos), llamar `task.wait()` una vez por tanda y armar cada tanda
  fuera del DataModel antes de asignarle `Parent`.
- **[BINARIO]** El proxy tiene un mensaje "Request timeout", pero el valor no es visible.
- **[OFICIAL]** Del lado de Claude Code, `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` fija el tiempo máximo por
  llamada y `MCP_TIMEOUT` el de arranque
  ([doc](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)).
- **[INFERENCIA]** Trata cada llamada como algo que debe terminar en pocos segundos. Si un
  código lanza un hilo con `task.spawn` que sigue vivo después de responder, no se sabe si
  sobrevive; hay que probarlo.

**Tamaño de respuesta**

- **[BINARIO]** Existen los topes `FIntExecuteLuauMaxStringLength` y
  `FIntExecuteLuauMaxJsonLength`; sus valores vienen del servidor de banderas y no se
  pudieron leer.
- **[OFICIAL]** Claude Code avisa cuando una respuesta MCP pasa de 10.000 tokens y la
  limita a 25.000 por defecto; se sube con `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS`.
- **[INFERENCIA]** Devuelve siempre resúmenes cortos (conteos, nombres), nunca volcados
  del árbol completo.

**Permisos del hilo**

- **[COMUNIDAD]** El código corre en un hilo con capacidades restringidas, no con
  identidad plena de plugin. En 0.741 no podía hacer `require` de ModuleScripts
  ([DevForum, 2026-10-02](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studios-mcp-executeluau-can-no-longer-require-modulescripts/4909614)).
  En 0.746 corría sin la capacidad `Network` y no podía asignar `Parent` a scripts.
- **[OFICIAL]** Personal de Roblox confirmó el arreglo de lo segundo: "we rolled out a fix
  for the script parenting issue" (versión mínima 0.746.0.7461269) el 2026-11-06, y el de
  HttpService el 2026-11-11
  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studio-mcp-executeluau-now-runs-without-the-network-capability-cant-parent-scripts-or-require-modules/4976763)).
- **[OFICIAL]** Problema conocido vigente: "In a place that hasn't been saved to Roblox,
  `execute_luau` can't make HTTP requests"

- **[OFICIAL]** Los permisos de Open Cloud, las carpetas de subida, el acceso a DataStore y
  las peticiones HTTP se conceden por juego en la pestaña MCP Permissions. Cada juego
  arranca en nivel "Balanced". Solo aplican a lugares de un juego publicado.

**Escribir scripts**

- **[OFICIAL]** Sí puede: `multi_edit` crea el script si no existe.
- **[BINARIO]** La descripción de `execute_luau` prohíbe usarlo para editar código: "DO NOT
  use this tool to edit, create, rename, or refactor the source of any Script... Setting

**Leer la salida**

- **[BINARIO]** "returns the value of the last expression" (como la barra de comandos).

**Cámara**

### 2.1 Respuestas cortas

| ¿Dos sesiones de Claude Code contra el **mismo** Studio sin pisarse? | Técnicamente se conectan, pero no hay ningún bloqueo ni aislamiento. No lo hagas. | BINARIO e INFERENCIA; pregunta sin respuesta oficial |

### 2.3 Lo reportado por la comunidad

- **A favor.** Un usuario que trabaja justo así: `studio_id` "has made running multiple

- **Fallo abierto.** Si se abre una ventana de Studio cuando `StudioMCP.exe` ya está

  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studiomcp-fails-to-list-studio-instances-after-new-studio-window-opens-while-studiomcp-is-already-running/4729586)).
- **Varios agentes sobre un mismo Studio.** "Last time I tried working with subagents they
  started fighting over the Studio MCP, will that ever work?" (2026-11-04, sin respuesta).
  Las preguntas directas a Roblox sobre este caso tampoco tuvieron respuesta.
- **Abrir varias ventanas.** Hay un reporte del 2026-08-18 de que abrir una ventana nueva
  cierra la anterior; Roblox contestó "We cannot reproduce this issue"
  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/studio-closes-existing-window-when-opening-a-new-one/4817979)).
  Otro reporte de 2025 muestra que existe un tope por memoria: "You've reached the limit
  for open Studio window. Please close some to free up memory."
  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/latest-studio-update-doesnt-allow-multiple-windows-open-at-the-same-time/3679128)).
- **Servidor viejo y bifurcaciones.**
  - `Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server`, archivado el 2026-04-03, usaba el puerto 44755 con una
    sola cola de comandos: no podía dirigirse a un Studio concreto
    ([GitHub](https://github.com/Roblox/studio-rust-mcp-server)).

### 2.4 Inferencias mías

- El aislamiento entre chats **no lo impone el servidor**: cualquier sesión puede escribir
  en cualquier Studio conectado con solo pasar otro `studio_id`. La seguridad depende de la
  disciplina del agente, así que hay que dársela por escrito y con una comprobación
  automática (ver 2.5).
- Dos sesiones sobre el mismo Studio comparten el hilo principal, el estado de juego
  (Play/Edit), la cámara, la selección y el historial de deshacer. Una puede detener la
  prueba que la otra está grabando. No hay forma de repartirlo.
- La sesión de Claude Code que arrancó primero es dueña del host. Si la cierras, las demás
  pierden la conexión unos segundos mientras otra toma el puerto.
- Las ventanas de Studio son procesos separados, así que una prueba en una no debería
  afectar a otra. Lo que sí comparten es GPU, CPU y memoria.
- La grabación es el único paso que no admite paralelo real: con dos o más Studio
  renderizando, el que se graba puede perder cuadros.

### 2.5 Arquitectura recomendada para 2 a 4 chats

**Regla base: un chat, una ventana de Studio, un lugar, una carpeta.**

1. **Una carpeta por video**, por ejemplo `videos/012-el-secreto/`, con el guion, la lista de
   planos, el audio y el lugar `012-el-secreto.rbxl`. Cada chat de Claude Code se abre en su
   carpeta.
2. **Nombres únicos.** El `name` que devuelve `list_roblox_studios` incluye el nombre del
   archivo o el id del lugar. Si cada lugar se llama distinto, el agente puede elegir sin
   ambigüedad. Nunca abras dos copias con el mismo nombre.
3. **Marca de identidad dentro del lugar.** Al crear el lugar desde la plantilla, guarda un
   atributo, por ejemplo `workspace:SetAttribute("VideoId", "012")`. El chat lo lee antes de
   cualquier tanda de cambios. Así se cubre el caso "un solo Studio conectado pero no es el
   mío".
4. **Protocolo de arranque escrito en el `CLAUDE.md` de cada carpeta de video:**
   - Llamar `list_roblox_studios` y elegir la instancia cuyo `name` contiene el nombre del
     archivo de esta carpeta. Si no aparece, detenerse y avisar; no usar otra.
   - Verificar el atributo `VideoId` con `execute_luau` (`datamodel_type: "Edit"`).
   - Pasar ese `studio_id` en todas las llamadas.
   - Si una llamada responde "not connected", volver a listar y repetir la verificación.
   - Prohibido usar un `studio_id` que no haya pasado la verificación.
5. **Orden de apertura**, para esquivar el fallo abierto de 2.3: abre primero todas las
   ventanas de Studio, activa el MCP en cada una y deja visible el panel de MCP; después
   abre los chats de Claude Code. Si agregas una ventana más tarde y no aparece en la
   lista, abre su panel de MCP o reinicia el chat.
6. **Servidor MCP registrado una sola vez con alcance `user`** (comando de 1.2). No hace
   falta un `.mcp.json` por video.
7. **Biblioteca compartida de solo lectura.** Caras, ropa, escenarios y el script director
   viven en una plantilla `plantilla.rbxl` y en un registro `biblioteca/recursos.json` con
   los id de recurso. Solo un chat (o tú) sube recursos nuevos; los chats de video solo
   leen el registro. Así no hay dos chats subiendo la misma cara ni chocando con el límite
   de subidas de la cuenta.
8. **Turno único de grabación.** Un archivo de bloqueo, por ejemplo `grabacion.lock` en la
   raíz del proyecto, con el número del video que está grabando. Un chat que va a grabar lo
   crea, y los demás no entran a modo juego ni lanzan trabajo pesado mientras exista. Lo
   ideal es que tú lances la grabación a mano, video por video.
9. **Ventanas a la vista.** No minimices las ventanas de Studio. **[BINARIO]** Para las
   capturas de paneles de plugin el propio Studio advierte que si la ventana está tapada o
   minimizada la captura devuelve lo que haya en pantalla en esa posición. Para el visor
   3D no hay dato; es prudente asumir lo mismo. Un segundo monitor ayuda mucho.
10. **Guardado.** Cada lugar es un archivo local `.rbxl`; `save_place` lo escribe sin
    diálogo, pero la primera vez hay que hacer Guardar como a mano (estado
    `NeedsUserAction`). Limitación: en lugares locales no publicados no hay
    `open_cloud_invoke` ni HTTP desde `execute_luau`. Si necesitas esas funciones, usa un
    solo juego privado publicado con un lugar por video.

Cuántos chats: con 16 GB de memoria, dos. Con 32 GB y tarjeta gráfica dedicada, hasta
cuatro en edición, grabando de a uno. Es una estimación mía; Roblox no publica consumo por
instancia.

### 2.6 Plan B: solo una instancia de Studio

Si en el equipo de casa no se sostienen varias ventanas (por el fallo de 2.3, por memoria o
porque el MCP no las lista), el paralelismo se mueve fuera de Studio:

- **Los chats trabajan en paralelo todo lo que no toca Studio**: guion, voz, tiempos por
  palabra, lista de planos en JSON, caras dibujadas, subtítulos y montaje con ffmpeg. Eso
  es la mayor parte del tiempo de un video.
- **Un solo chat "operador de Studio"** atiende una cola: toma la carpeta del siguiente
  video, abre su lugar, carga la lista de planos, revisa encuadres, graba, guarda y pasa al
  siguiente. Como el video es datos (JSON) sobre una plantilla común, el tiempo dentro de
  Studio por video es corto.
- La cola puede ser una carpeta `cola-studio/` con un archivo por video y un estado
  (`pendiente`, `en-studio`, `grabado`).
- La Ruta B de `docs/03` (render en código, sin Studio) queda como segundo respaldo y sí es
  paralela sin límite.

## 3. Personajes R6 por script

### 3.1 Crear el rig

- **[OFICIAL]** `Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescriptionAsync(description, rigType,
  assetTypeVerification)` devuelve un `Model` de personaje R6 o R15 según `rigType`.
  Suspende la ejecución (Yields) y su seguridad es `None`
  ([referencia](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Players#CreateHumanoidModelFromDescriptionAsync)).
  La variante sin `Async` (`CreateHumanoidModelFromDescription`) sigue existiendo, pero la
  referencia dice que fue reemplazada por la `Async` y que esta es la que debe usarse.
- **[OFICIAL]** Para copiar un avatar real:
  `Players:GetHumanoidDescriptionFromUserIdAsync(userId)` y
  `Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromUserIdAsync(userId)`.
- **[OFICIAL]** La herramienta manual ahora se llama **Rig Generator** (antes Rig Builder):
  pestaña Avatar o Home, botón Character; inserta un R6 o R15 con el nombre `Rig`. La doc
  advierte que la ropa y los accesorios en capas solo se pueden equipar en R15
  ([doc](https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/rig-builder)).
- **[COMUNIDAD]** Estos métodos funcionan en modo edición: es lo que usan los plugins de
  tipo "Load Character"
  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/load-character-plugin/1848301)).
- **[INFERENCIA]** Desde `execute_luau` deberían funcionar igual, pero el hilo tiene
  capacidades restringidas (ver 1.4) y estos métodos descargan recursos. Es la primera
  prueba del piloto. Si fallan, el respaldo es insertar un R6 una sola vez con Rig
  Generator, guardarlo en la plantilla y clonarlo por script.

```lua
-- execute_luau, datamodel_type = "Edit"
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local desc = Instance.new("HumanoidDescription")
desc.HeadColor = Color3.fromRGB(245, 205, 48)
desc.TorsoColor = Color3.fromRGB(13, 105, 172)
desc.LeftArmColor = Color3.fromRGB(245, 205, 48)
desc.RightArmColor = Color3.fromRGB(245, 205, 48)
desc.LeftLegColor = Color3.fromRGB(40, 127, 71)
desc.RightLegColor = Color3.fromRGB(40, 127, 71)

local rig = Players:CreateHumanoidModelFromDescriptionAsync(desc, Enum.HumanoidRigType.R6)
rig.Name = "Actor_Ana"
rig:PivotTo(CFrame.new(0, 3, 0))
rig.Parent = workspace

local root = rig:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
if root then
	root.Anchored = true -- para que no se caiga ni camine al entrar a modo juego
end

game:GetService("ChangeHistoryService"):SetWaypoint("Crear Actor_Ana")
return rig:GetFullName()
```

### 3.2 Vestirlo

- **[OFICIAL]** `HumanoidDescription` tiene, entre otras, las propiedades `Shirt`, `Pants`,
  `GraphicTShirt`, `Face`, `HatAccessory`, `HairAccessory`, `FaceAccessory`,
  `NeckAccessory`, `ShouldersAccessory`, `FrontAccessory`, `BackAccessory`,
  `WaistAccessory` y los colores del cuerpo. Los accesorios son texto con id separados por
  coma. `SetAccessories(accessories, includeRigidAccessories)` acepta una tabla
  ([referencia](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/HumanoidDescription),
  [guía](https://create.roblox.com/docs/characters/appearance)).
- **[OFICIAL]** Para cambiar la apariencia de un rig ya creado:
  `Humanoid:ApplyDescriptionAsync(desc)`; si el personaje se modificó por otros medios,
  `Humanoid:ApplyDescriptionResetAsync(desc)`.
- **[INFERENCIA, conocimiento general de la plataforma]** `Shirt` y `Pants` en
  `HumanoidDescription` esperan el id del artículo de ropa del catálogo, no el id de la
  imagen. Para ropa propia sin publicarla en el catálogo, crea las instancias directamente:
  la clase `Shirt` tiene la propiedad `ShirtTemplate` y `Pants` tiene `PantsTemplate`, que
  reciben el id de una imagen subida por ti.

```lua
local shirt = rig:FindFirstChildOfClass("Shirt") or Instance.new("Shirt")
shirt.ShirtTemplate = "rbxassetid://ID_DE_TU_IMAGEN"
shirt.Parent = rig
```

### 3.3 Posarlo sin animación

- **[OFICIAL]** `Motor6D.Transform` es la propiedad que mueve un `Animator`. Sus cambios no
  se aplican de inmediato sino en lote antes del paso de física, y si el modelo tiene un
  `Animator` con animaciones, este la sobrescribe en cada cuadro. Además está marcada
  `Hidden` y `NotReplicated`
  ([referencia](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Motor6D#Transform)).
- **[OFICIAL]** `C0` y `C1` sí se aplican de inmediato (la misma página lo contrasta).
- **[INFERENCIA]** Para poses fijas la opción robusta es **`C0`**: se ve al instante en
  edición, se guarda con el lugar y ningún `Animator` la pisa. `Transform` no se guarda y
  en edición puede no refrescarse. Guarda el `C0` original en un atributo para poder volver
  a la pose neutra. Si el rig trae un script `Animate`, bórralo para que no cargue
  animaciones de reposo al entrar a modo juego.
- **[COMUNIDAD, conocimiento general]** En R6 las articulaciones están dentro de `Torso` y
  se llaman `Neck`, `Left Shoulder`, `Right Shoulder`, `Left Hip`, `Right Hip`; `RootJoint`
  está en `HumanoidRootPart`. Por la orientación de sus `C0`, el eje que levanta un brazo
  hacia adelante no es el que uno espera; hay que encontrarlo una vez con capturas y
  dejarlo fijo en una tabla de poses.

```lua
local function posar(rig, nombre, giro)
	local torso = rig:FindFirstChild("Torso")
	local motor = torso and torso:FindFirstChild(nombre)
	if not motor or not motor:IsA("Motor6D") then
		return false
	end
	local base = motor:GetAttribute("C0Base")
	if base == nil then
		base = motor.C0
		motor:SetAttribute("C0Base", base)
	end
	motor.C0 = base * giro
	return true
end

-- Brazo derecho levantado (el eje exacto se confirma con una captura)
posar(workspace.Actor_Ana, "Right Shoulder", CFrame.Angles(0, 0, math.rad(90)))
-- Cabeza inclinada
posar(workspace.Actor_Ana, "Neck", CFrame.Angles(math.rad(-15), 0, 0))
```

### 3.4 Cambiar la cara

- **[COMUNIDAD]** En R6 la cara es un `Decal` llamado `face` dentro de `Head`
  ([DevForum](https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-to-import-high-quality-character-faces-on-roblox-characters-works-with-r15-and-r6/622433)).
- **[OFICIAL]** `Decal.Texture` está marcada como obsoleta: "This property has been
  deprecated. Use `ColorMapContent` for future work." El tipo nuevo es `Content`, con
  `Content.fromAssetId(id)` y `Content.fromUri(uri)`
  ([Decal](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/Decal),
  [Content](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/datatypes/Content)). El formato
  `rbxassetid://ID` sigue siendo el estándar para recursos subidos
  ([doc de recursos](https://create.roblox.com/docs/projects/assets)).

```lua
local function ponerCara(rig, assetId)
	local head = rig:FindFirstChild("Head")
	if not head then
		return false
	end
	local cara = head:FindFirstChild("face")
	if not cara then
		cara = Instance.new("Decal")
		cara.Name = "face"
		cara.Face = Enum.NormalId.Front
		cara.Parent = head
	end
	cara.ColorMapContent = Content.fromAssetId(assetId)
	-- Forma antigua, todavía funcional: cara.Texture = "rbxassetid://" .. assetId
	return true
end
```

- **[INFERENCIA]** Para que el cambio de cara no parpadee en la grabación, carga antes
  todas las caras con `ContentProvider:PreloadAsync` y, mejor aún, deja un `Decal` por
  expresión en la cabeza y alterna su `Transparency` entre 0 y 1.

**Subir caras propias**

- **[OFICIAL y BINARIO]** `upload_image` recibe **URLs HTTP**, no rutas locales. Para
  imágenes en disco hay que servirlas por HTTP (por ejemplo `python -m http.server 8123` en
  la carpeta de caras y pasar `http://localhost:8123/susto.png`). Devuelve un mapa de ruta
  a `rbxassetid://...`.
- **[OFICIAL]** Alternativa: `open_cloud_invoke` con `files`, que sí sube archivos locales,
  pero exige un lugar de un juego publicado, los permisos `asset:read` y `asset:write`, y
  que la carpeta esté aprobada en MCP Permissions. El agente no puede copiar archivos a una
  carpeta aprobada para saltarse esa restricción
  ([doc](https://create.roblox.com/docs/studio/mcp-open-cloud)).
- **[OFICIAL]** `store_image` **no sube nada**: solo convierte un archivo local en un URI
  para herramientas de generación.
- **[OFICIAL]** Moderación: "Roblox performs both human and automated asset moderation".
  Las subidas son permanentes, quedan a nombre del dueño del juego y Open Cloud no puede
  borrarlas. Los recursos son privados por defecto
  ([doc](https://create.roblox.com/docs/projects/assets#asset-moderation)).
- **Tiempos de moderación**: no encontré ninguna cifra oficial. **[INFERENCIA]** Sube el
  paquete completo de caras un día antes de grabar y verifica en Studio que todas cargan.
  Las caras deben ser PNG con transparencia; evita cualquier rasgo que la moderación pueda
  leer como contenido inapropiado.

- **[OFICIAL]** Sí existe una vía: `Animator:StepAnimations(deltaTime)` avanza las
